reports.title_original: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

summary:
Several female Dutch public figures are considering legal action after manipulated pornographic videos featuring their faces appeared on a website with 13 million monthly visitors. The videos include Dutch artists, TV presenters, Olympic athletes, former ministers, mayors, and members of the royal family. Caretaker Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to report them. Some managers and spokespeople confirmed to NOS that reports have been filed or legal steps are being considered, though names are withheld for safety.

Deepfake pornography is illegal under revenge porn laws. Lawyers advise victims to file police reports, after which prosecutors can try to take the site offline. Other options include a mass claim, a complaint to the Dutch data protection authority, or contacting hosting companies. The article notes a previous case where a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort received a 180-hour suspended community service sentence for making deepfake porn of presenter Welmoed Sijtsma.
